newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL-GMexico Q2 to trail year-ago, beat Q1.
newsitem.headline: POLL-GMexico Q2 to trail year-ago, beat Q1.

text.p: Grupo Mexico SA (GMexico), the country's largest copper producer, is seen reporting shiny second quarter earnings compared with a dull first three months because of higher metals prices, analysts said, but the results are called a tad lower than the same period a year earlier, when GMexico posted an unadjusted 1.237 peso/share.
A survey of four analysts polled by Reuters gave an average forecast of 1.06 pesos per/share against the 0.86 peso per share reported in the first quarter.
Bullish-trending copper prices were the top factor seen impacting the expected quarter-over-quarter rise in earnings.
"Copper prices are at their best levels since the first quarter of 1996. This is what is going to hit the bottom line the most," mining analyst Christopher Albi said.

The rise in copper prices year over year is not as dramatic as between the first and second quarters of this year, analysts noted. But year-over-year earnings should be slightly lower, in part because of margins, they said.
"The difference between this and that quarter will be margins," Albi said.
The 37.6 percent operating margin in last year's second quarter would likely drop down slightly to 35 percent, in part due to higher fuel costs, Albi predicted.

Albi added he had calculated average copper LME prices at $2,505 per metric tonne in the second quarter of this year against $2,485 per tonne for the like period a year earlier. But in the first quarter of this year, copper prices were $2,423 per tonne, he added, largely still down as a result of the Sumitomo trading scandal.
The 1996 Sumitomo copper trading debacle, which cost the Japanese metals giant Sumitomo Corp $2.6 billion, sent world prices of the metal plummeting in the second half of 1996.
David Bodenberg, a consultant to Credit Lyonnais, agreed that GMexico's results would come through stronger than the first quarter's, with copper prices the main factor.

Some analysts also looked to probable higher sales volumes and lower production costs as other fundamentals boosting second quarter earnings as an expanded 300,000 tonne per year copper smelter is now in operation at La Caridad.

"Sales volumes will be a little higher this quarter (against Q1 1997) because of the expansion at La Caridad," said Hector Novoa, analyst at Serfin brokerage's Mexico City office. "Production costs should also be lower."

Between March and April, GMexico eased on line its expanded its anode copper smelter now with a capacity of 300,000 tonnes/year from 180,000 tonnes previously. GMexico told Reuters recently it has been working at operating levels of 95-96 percent.
Albi said he thought bullish zinc prices would also add a couple of centavos to the earnings this quarter.
He calculated zinc prices in the period had gone up 26 percent since the same period in 1996.
GMexico's 1996 sales came 61 percent from copper and 14 percent from zinc. Silver sales contributed 15 percent, according to the company's annual report.

Bodenberg said the broader picture going forward was crucial for GMexico after an important second quarter acquisition. In June, the company led a consortium to purchase Mexico's Pacific-North and Topolobampo-Ojinaga railways at auction for $527.39 million.

"What is going to be interesting is how and when GMexico has to pony up the money for the railroads," Bodenberg said. "That is going to make big differences to GMexico's cash and non-cash items," he added.

GMexico has still not detailed how it plans to finance the acquisition. It holds a 74 percent stake in the consortium, called Grupo Ferroviaria Mexicana. Mexican builder Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora SA de CV and U.S.-based Union Pacific Corp each has a 13 percent holding.
